MACS3 3.0.5 (Model-based Analysis of ChIP-Seq), with hmmlearn 0.3.3: macs3
Licences: MACS3 is under the BSD 3-clause licence (LICENSE in this folder, MACS3's own); the fermi-lite, ksw and swalign
code in it under MIT, and SIMDe under MIT and CC0 (scientific-notices/macs3/). hmmlearn: BSD 3-clause
(scientific-notices/hmmlearn/). Their compiled parts were generated by Cython (cython-notices/); hmmlearn's C++ uses the
pybind11 headers (scientific-notices/pybind11/). THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt lists every part.
The Python they run in is Pyodide 314.0.7 – CPython 3.14.2 compiled with Emscripten 5.0.3 – in ../../pyodide/314.0.7/,
unchanged (the one copy that Cutadapt and Bracken use too), with the packages of Pyodide's own distribution that MACS3
needs next to it, unchanged: NumPy 2.4.6, SciPy 1.18.0, pandas 3.0.2, scikit-learn 1.8.0, h5py 3.13.0, joblib 1.5.3,
threadpoolctl 3.6.0, python-dateutil 2.9.0.post0, pytz 2026.1.post1, tzdata 2025.3, six 1.17.0, packaging 26.1 and
pkgconfig 1.6.0. In wheels/, with MACS3's and hmmlearn's: AnnData 0.10.9, array-api-compat 1.11.2 and natsort 8.4.0, pure
Python, as released on PyPI. These packages are under BSD, MIT and Apache 2.0 licences; their licence files, and those
of the libraries compiled into some of them – OpenBLAS with LAPACK and libf2c, Boost, HDF5 1.12.1 and zlib – are in
scientific-notices/ (a folder for each, and one for each wheel; scientific-notices/README.md and manifest.json say where
each file came from). runtime-notices/ holds the notices of the Python itself (CPython, Emscripten, libffi, hiwire, xz,
zstd, SQLite, bzip2, zlib), as for Cutadapt. Pyodide and hiwire are under the Mozilla Public License 2.0, and so are
the recipes with which Pyodide built its packages: their source code is in ../../../licenses/sources/
(pyodide-314.0.7.tar.gz, hiwire-6a1e67280a15d929ebeceee54a6358c9c8d5f697.tar.gz, pyodide-recipes-314-20260911.tar.gz).
Upstream sources: MACS3 https://github.com/macs3-project/MACS (macs3-3.0.5.tar.gz on PyPI), hmmlearn
https://github.com/hmmlearn/hmmlearn (hmmlearn-0.3.3.tar.gz on PyPI), the others on PyPI; Pyodide
https://github.com/pyodide/pyodide (release 314.0.7) and https://github.com/pyodide/pyodide-recipes (314-20260911).

Built by the genomics-wasm project (https://github.com/comparativechrono/genomics-wasm, commit c977980): MACS3's Cython
and C extensions and hmmlearn's C++ compiled to WebAssembly with pyodide-build (Emscripten 5.0.3) for CPython 3.14.2,
into the wheels in wheels/. manifest.json names every package – Pyodide's and these – with its SHA-256, and macs3.py,
MACS3's command line (bin/macs3 of its release, unchanged), with its own. The page checks them all, and that Pyodide's
catalogue gives the same versions, files and SHA-256 for Pyodide's packages, before Python loads any of them. Each
command runs in a worker of its own (assets/js/python-worker.mjs, adapted from genomics-wasm's runtime/macs3-execute.mjs):
it starts that Python, installs the packages in the manifest's order and runs macs3.py with the command's arguments.
Everything needed to build it again is described in ../../../licenses/genomics-wasm-build/ (tools/macs3/,
workbench/build-macs3-for-workbench.sh).

The changes to the source (tools/macs3/ there). browser.patch: BAM and BAI virtual offsets are kept as 64-bit numbers,
as on Linux (on wasm32 they were cut to 32 bits); the messages say "[RSS unavailable]" where Linux gives the memory used
(WebAssembly has no resource module); the two process pools of callvar become maps over the same parts, one after
another, in the same order – callvar -m N computes the same, in one process; an unused test main() is renamed.
integer-width.patch: sums of fragment lengths, q-value ranks and weighted counts are kept 64-bit, as on Linux.
hmmlearn-wasm.patch: a floating-point status flag that WebAssembly does not have is not cleared. No formula, cutoff or
rounding is changed.

Checked against MACS3 3.0.5 on CPython 3.14.2 for Linux, both unchanged and with these changes (genomics-wasm's
comparison, scripts/validate-macs3.mjs, Node.js 22: 39 of 39 cases – all fourteen commands, with MACS's own test data:
CTCF ChIP-seq of human chromosome 22, single-end and paired, a single-cell fragment file, yeast ATAC-seq, and the reads
of its callvar test): 99 of the 103 result files the same byte for byte – peaks, summits, bedGraph tracks, tables,
states, variant calls –, and the other four, models, the same but for their last decimals (the cross-correlation in the
R scripts of callpeak's and predictd's model, the trained HMMs of hmmratac: at most 1.3e-12, relative). In the
workbench, with the example data, the results were compared with native MACS3 once more – see ../../../../THIRD_PARTY.md.
